ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: Ethical approval for the study was received from the Institutional Review Boards of the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) (Approval number 2020 For participants younger than 18 years, written consent was obtained from a parent or caretakers, and assent was additionally obtained from participants aged 12-17 years.

-009), the University of Ibadan/ University College Hospital Ethics Committee (Approval Number UI/EC/21/0190), Oyo State Health Research Ethics Committee (Approval Number NHREC/OYOSHRIEC/10/11/12) and OLACH Ethics Committee (Approval Number OC/EC/21/10).

Patients with Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi), Salmonella enterica serovar Paratyphi (S. Paratyphi), invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS), or typhoid gastrointestinal perforation (special cases) were enrolled, with malaria patients serving as controls.
Participants were classified into five case-type categories: S. Typhi, S. Paratyphi, iNTS, special (perforation) cases, and malaria for controls.

At the time of the first interview, participants were interviewed regarding all direct medical and non-medical out-of-pocket expenditures, income losses, substitute laborer costs, and caretaker costs incurred up to the day before the interview, and socioeconomic information such as household income and expenditure was also collected.

To minimize recall bias, participants were provided with a diary card to record treatment-related costs, additional healthcare visits, productivity losses, and support from substitute laborers or caregivers between interviews.
These participants were assigned to the most comparable income group and imputed with the mean income of that group.

Ethical approval for the study was received from the Institutional Review Boards of the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) (Approval number 2020 For participants younger than 18 years, written consent was obtained from a parent or caretakers, and assent was additionally obtained from participants aged 12-17 years.
Patients enrolled in the COI studies, provided written informed consent.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
